File No. PS26-27131
Resolution approving a Public Emergency Medical Transportation Letter of Agreement between the City of Tampa and State Of Florida Agency for Health Care Administration to authorize payment of Intergovernmental Transfers to the State in the amount of Two Million Three Hundred Thirty-One Thousand and Seven Hundred Sixty-Three 71/100 dollars ($2,331,763.71) and receive an estimated Five Million Two Hundred Thirty-One Thousand Six Hundred and Eighty-Eight 82/100 Dollars ($5,231,688.82) for Emergency Medical Transportation; Authorizing the execution thereof by the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. PS26-27131
Resolution approving a Public Emergency Medical Transportation Letter of Agreement between the City of Tampa and State Of Florida Agency for Health Care Administration to authorize payment of Intergovernmental Transfers to the State in the amount of Two Million Three Hundred Thirty-One Thousand and Seven Hundred Sixty-Three 71/100 dollars ($2,331,763.71) and receive an estimated Five Million Two Hundred Thirty-One Thousand Six Hundred and Eighty-Eight 82/100 Dollars ($5,231,688.82) for Emergency Medical Transportation; Authorizing the execution thereof by the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
As set forth in the attached Public Emergency Medical Transportation Letter of Agreement (herein "Letter of Agreement"} between the City of Tampa and the State of Florida, Agency for Health Care Administration, the parties have authorized a supplemental payment program for Medicaid managed care patients who are transported to the hospital by public emergency medical transportation providers.

The State of Florida Legislature has authorized a continuation of the supplemental payment program to include Medicaid Managed Care transports for the purpose of leveraging intergovernmental funds with a 57 percent (57%) federal share and 43 percent (43%) City share that Medicaid Managed Care providers will later reimburse.

By participating in the supplemental payment program for Medicaid managed care patients as outlined in the Letter of Agreement, City of Tampa Fire Rescue can substantially increase its Medicaid managed care patient transport revenue with the City contributing $2,331,763.71 as its share of the State's total federal match requirement and receive approximately $5,231,688.82 of Managed Care Option (MCO) patient transport revenue for an overall net revenue increase to the City of approximately $2,899,925.11 which is included within the City's annual budget.

SubjectA resolution appropriating funds for the five year tree canopy survey.
Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
A resolution making certain changes in the Budget of the City of Tampa for the 
fiscal year ending September 30, 2027; approving the transfer, reallocation, 
and/or appropriation of $240,000 from the Central Tampa Tree Trust Fund, 
Westshore Tampa Tree Trust Fund, University Tampa Tree Trust Fund, New 
Tampa Tree Trust Fund, South Tampa Tree Trust Fund; providing an effective 
date.
BACKGROUND:
The City of Tampa wishes to conduct a new instance of the Tree Canopy Study. The tree 
canopy analysis identifies the extent of the existing tree canopy, the potential for new tree 
plantings, and provides a way to measure tree canopy coverage over time.  Using satellite 
imagery, researchers measure  and assess the condition of the city's urban forest, as well as 
the social and economic benefits provided by trees. Survey crews also collect field data from 
sample sites to verify the satellite imagery. This information will help strategically plan and 
target resources for the greatest return on investment in our tree canopy, including reduced 
stormwater runoff and reduced energy consumption.
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes
FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
This resolution appropriates funds in the amount of $240,000 for the five year tree canopy 
survey for use by the Parks and Recreation Department within the Various Tree Trust Funds.

agendaItems.background: The Copeland Park Veteran’s Memorial is the third Veteran’s Memorial recently designed and constructed by the City of Tampa Parks and Recreation Department. The memorial includes a brick plaza with a memorial structure, created by an artist, and benches.  The plaza is surrounded by trees and plantings that provide enclosure and provide a respite and calm atmosphere for contemplation. This funding request is to cover the cost of several large southern live oaks and bald cypress. The oaks will provide shade in areas near the plaza, and the cypress will be evenly spaced at the perimeter to provide a stately presence.

SubjectA resolution appropriating funding for the planting and irrigation of trees at the 
Copeland Park Veteran's Memorial.
Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
A resolution making certain changes in the budget of the City of Tampa for the 
Fiscal Year ending September 30, 2027; approving the Transfer, Reallocation, 
and/or appropriation of $28,556.64 within the University Tampa Tree Trust 
Fund; providing an effective date.
BACKGROUND:
The Copeland Park Veteran’s Memorial is the third Veteran’s Memorial recently designed and 
constructed by the City of Tampa Parks and Recreation Department. The memorial includes 
a brick plaza with a memorial structure, created by an artist, and benches.  The plaza is 
surrounded by trees and plantings that provide enclosure and provide a respite and calm 
atmosphere for contemplation. This funding request is to cover the cost of several large 
southern live oaks and bald cypress. The oaks will provide shade in areas near the plaza, and 
the cypress will be evenly spaced at the perimeter to provide a stately presence.
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes
FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
This resolution appropriates funds for the planting and irrigation of trees at the Copeland Park 
Veteran's Memorial in the amount of $28,556.64 for use by the Parks and Recreation 
Department within the University Tampa Tree Trust Fund.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. NCA26-27130

agendaItems.background:
1. Department / Location of Project: Neighborhood Enhancement Division — Neighborhood Enhancement Division

2. Total vendors accessed and downloaded the proposal: 34

3. Number and List of proposers: Two, Republic Services of Florida, Limited Partnership, dba Republic Services of Tampa & Waste Connections of Florida, Inc.

4. Agreement Amount: $202,000

5. Why the winning proposal was selected: The evaluation committee selected the most responsible and responsive Proposer whose proposal meets the needs of the City to the best degree.

It is recommended that the City award Class III Waste Disposal (Bid Discount) to Republic Services of Florida, Limited Partnership, dba Republic Services of Tampa for use by Neighborhood Enhancement. The term of the agreement is for a (1) one-year term with (3) three additional (1) one-year renewal options. The Department has reviewed and approved the proposal response from Republic Services of Florida, Limited Partnership, dba Republic Services of Tampa and comments were supplied via Department recommendation letter.

Equal Business Opportunity: Pursuant to the review by the Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Division, it was determined that the EBO Bid Discount provision would apply in the bid specifications to eligible City of Tampa Certified firms.

SubjectResolution assessing the costs expended by the City to abate (2) properties:

Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
A resolution assessing the costs expended by the City of Tampa, a municipal 
corporation, for the preparation, demolition and/or removal of certain buildings 
and/or structures from the following properties:  (1) 6211 S Martindale Ave, 
and (2) 2904 N 17th St, after the determination that said building or structure 
satisfied the criteria to demolish and the property owner(s) failed to demolish 
and/or remove same or failed to do so prior to the City incurring costs; 
authorizing a certified copy of the resolution to be recorded with the Clerk of 
the Circuit Court and having the force and effect of a notice of assessment of 
lien; providing an effective date.
BACKGROUND:
This resolution assesses the costs ($15,708.00) expended by the City of Tampa, including 
administrative costs, for the preparation, demolition and/or removal of buildings and/or 
structures on the properties described in Exhibit “A” of the Resolution that satisfied the criteria 
to demolish set forth in Section 19-5(a)(2) & (b)(1), City of Tampa Code of Ordinances when 
the property owner(s) failed to demolish and/or remove the unsafe building and/or structure 
within the time allowed or failed to do so prior to the City incurring said costs.
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes
FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
To impose lien in an effort to recover the required administrative fee and hard costs expended 
by the City.  Revenue will be received by the Neighborhood Enhancement Division within the 
General Fund.

Resolution approving an Agreement for Design-Build Initial Services in the amount of $524,300 between the City of Tampa and Bandes Construction Company, Inc. in connection with Contract 26-C-00025 Washington Street Park and Curtis Hixon Waterfront Park Design-Build; authorizing the Mayor of the City of Tampa to execute same; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. INF26-27132
Resolution approving an Agreement for Design-Build Initial Services in the amount of $524,300 between the City of Tampa and Bandes Construction Company, Inc. in connection with Contract 26-C-00025 Washington Street Park and Curtis Hixon Waterfront Park Design-Build; authorizing the Mayor of the City of Tampa to execute same; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
1. Contract Title: 26-C-00025 Washington Street Park and Curtis Hixon Waterfront Park Design-Build a. Address of Project: Curtis Hixon Park 600 N Ashley Drive Tampa, FL 33602 and Washington Street Park 118 N 12th St Tampa, FL 33602 b. Number of bidders/submitters: 4 c. Names of bidders/submitters: Bandes Construction Company, Inc.

Wharton-Smith, Inc.

Hennessy Construction Services, Corp Biltmore Construction Co., Inc d. Dollar amount: $524,300 e.Why the awardee was selected: Selected Pursuant to FS 287.055 CCNA (Consultants’ Competitive Negotiation Act).

2. Contractor/Firm: Bandes Construction Company, Inc.

3.Business Case: Curtis Hixon Waterfront Park is one of the city's premier special event parks contributing to the city's economy and culture. Improvements to the paving, event lawn, and bathrooms are necessary to continue to support events and improve durability and safety. The project also includes improvements for existing canopy trees and the installation of new canopy trees for environmental, economic, and quality of life benefits.

Washington Street Park and the adjacent streetscape will be renovated to maximize public space for public benefit; improve maintainability; improve durability; improve functionality; increase recreation and place making opportunities; increase tree canopy; improve stormwater runoff treatment and conveyance; and respond to changing demographics and needs of the Channelside community based on public engagement.

4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: Bandes Construction Company, Inc., the prime contractor, is committed to utilizing two (2) city-certified firms for subcontracting.

5. Sustainability and Resiliency: All new construction for this project shall make the best use of all applicable and sustainable materials and methodologies to reduce operating costs.

6. Community Engagement: The Contract Administration Department (CAD) and Construction, Engineering and Inspection (CEI) division will assist the Contractor in the communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Build project. A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) 240 consecutive calendar days.

d.  The e-Builder project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

agendaItems.rawTitle:

agendaItems.background: The City and Manhattan Avenue, LLC entered into a settlement agreement in Case No. 23-CA-15073, under which Manhattan Avenue, LLC agreed to convey certain property to the City. A corrected warranty deed will convey Lots 1–9 to the City, while the proposed quitclaim deed will reconvey Lots 10–18 to correct the chain of title.

the CBA, debt service on the note will be paid from a combination of Downtown CRA Tax 
Increment Financing (TIF) revenues and the annual contribution from Hillsborough County of 
Tourist Development Taxes.  
The FY2026 adopted budget appropriated TIF revenues to fully pay for the annual debt 
service payment of the Series 2021A note.  As the City has received TDT revenue in the

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. DEO26-27182 (Part 1 of 2)(See Item )
Resolution of the City of Tampa, Florida, approving a Federal Award (No. ED26ATL0G0342) between the City of Tampa and the United States Department of Commerce, Economic Development Administration, for acceptance of grant funds in an amount not to exceed $280,000.00 to support the Tampa Resilient Industries Action Plan; Authorizing execution thereof by the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
The City of Tampa applied for and was awarded funding from the U.S. Economic Development Administration's FY2025 Disaster Supplemental Grant Program to support the production of a Tampa Resilient Industries Action Plan in the amount of up to $280,000.00.

The required match for this project is $70,000.00 for a total project cost of $350,000.00. The Tampa Resilient Industries Action Plan is a forward-looking strategy designed to enhance resilience and improve economic outcomes in land designated for industrial use and in other areas that support our target industries. This study will provide the foundation for implementation-ready projects that promote business continuity, disaster preparedness, and long-term economic competitiveness. By identifying vulnerabilities and opportunities, the Action Plan will position Tampa to attract investment, incentivize job growth, and build a stronger, more adaptable economy that can withstand future impacts.

File No. DEO26-27184 (Part 1 of 2)(See Item )
Resolution approving a purchase agreement for state tax credits between the City of Tampa, Florida, and U.S. Bank National Association, together with associated closing documents, which provide for the sale of Florida Voluntary Cleanup (“Brownsfield”) Tax Credits by the City of Tampa to U.S. Bank National Association for a purchase price of $196,286.14 (less associated broker’s fees for a net purchase price of $191,058.84); authorizing the execution thereof by the Mayor and attestation by the City Clerk; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. DEO26-27184 (Part 1 of 2)(See Item )
Resolution approving a purchase agreement for state tax credits between the City of Tampa, Florida, and U.S. Bank National Association, together with associated closing documents, which provide for the sale of Florida Voluntary Cleanup (“Brownsfield”) Tax Credits by the City of Tampa to U.S. Bank National Association for a purchase price of $196,286.14 (less associated broker’s fees for a net purchase price of $191,058.84); authorizing the execution thereof by the Mayor and attestation by the City Clerk; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
The Florida Legislature created the Voluntary Cleanup Tax Credit (VCTC) to encourage participants to conduct voluntary cleanup of certain drycleaning solvent contaminated sites and brownfield sites in designated brownfield areas.  Participants must meet the eligibility criteria established in the Florida Statute and must enter into a voluntary cleanup agreement with the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP).  If costs are eligible for a tax credit, the participant could claim 50% of the cost for solid waste removal, but not to exceed $500,000.

Since 2015, the City has been awarded 26 VCTC certificates with a combined tax credit value of $3.2 million, from which $3.0 million have been sold.  The City currently has five tax credits related to Hanna Avenue, Main Street Park, Cypress Housing Project, Channelside Drive Park, and East Hillsborough Avenue and Shadowlawn Avenue brownfield site rehabilitation projects totaling $209,931.70 that are available for sale.

As the City, being a tax-exempt entity, has no ability to utilize the Tax Credits to offset its tax obligations, the City has engaged Clocktower Tax Credits, LLC. to locate a purchaser for these Tax Credits.  Resolution 2023-798 approved the agreement between the City of Tampa and Clocktower Tax Credits, LLC. to provide brokerage services for the marketing and selling of VCTCs issued by FDEP to the City.  Clocktower Tax Credits, LLC. solicited proposals and has recommended U.S. Bank National Association as having submitted the best proposal.

The agreement will accept the U.S. Bank National Association proposal of $0.935 per dollar of tax credit sold, which will result in proceeds of $196,286.14. After agent fees of $5,227.30, or $0.0249 per dollar of tax credit sold, the City will receive $191,058.84 net, or $0.91 per dollar of tax credit sold.

agendaItems.background:
The City of Tampa currently uses the WebTMA Systems platform for the enterprise and asset management system for various departments. WebTMA’s Subscription Service allows organizations to lease the software while continuing to own their data.

Logistics and Asset Management along with the transition to the subscription service would also like to purchase the Capital Planning module to better manage their facilities records and the Data Analytics module for their operational and executive reporting and dashboarding.

Equal Business Opportunity: There was no EBO participation, as this purchase is being made under a standardization.

agendaItems.background:

Central Avenue, Tampa, Fl (“Development Agreement”).  As part of the development, a private stormwater pipe will be crossing North Avon Avenue, which is a public right of way.

The Development Agreement requires that the Developer obtain a franchise from the City in order to allow the stormwater pipe to cross the right of way.

SubjectAn Ordinance granting to Robles Park, LLC, Robles Park Village Development 
Group, LLC, RPV Parcel D, L.P., its successors and assigns, a non-exclusive 
franchise to use a portion of North Avon Avenue, in the City of Tampa.
Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
An Ordinance granting to Robles Park, LLC, Robles Park Village Development 
Group, LLC, RPV Parcel D, L.P., its successors and assigns, a non-exclusive 
franchise to use a portion of North Avon Avenue, in the City of Tampa to 
construct, access and maintain stormwater improvements and prescribing the 
terms and conditions under which said non-exclusive franchise may be 
exercised; providing for severability; providing an effective date.
BACKGROUND:
The City and Robles Park, LLC, Robles Park Village Development Group, LLC, and Open 
Space Acquisitions, LLC (collectively, the “Developer”) entered into a Development 
Agreement, dated September 5, 2024, regarding the development of property located on N. 
Central Avenue, Tampa, Fl (“Development Agreement”).  As part of the development, a 
private stormwater pipe will be crossing North Avon Avenue, which is a public right of way. 
The Development Agreement requires that the Developer obtain a franchise from the City in 
order to allow the stormwater pipe to cross the right of way.
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes
FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
This ordinance approves an agreement between the City of Tampa and Robles Park, LLC, 
Robles Park Village Development Group, LLC, and Open Space Acquisitions, LLC to use a 
portion of the right of way located within North Avon Avenue to construct, access, and 
maintain Stormwater Improvements. The City will collect a franchise fee in the amount of 
$2,500 in FY2027, with a 3% annual increase over a 20 year period for a total of $67,175.94. 
These funds will be collected by the Stormwater Department and deposited within the 
Stormwater Service Assessment Fund.

File No. INF26-26855 (Placed under Staff Reports and Unfinished Business pursuant to a motion made by Council.)
Resolution approving a Design-Build Services Agreement with a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP-1) for Contract 24-C-09003-GMP01 FY24 Citywide Distribution Watermain Improvements Design-Build between the City of Tampa and Westra Construction Corp., in the amount of $19,890,062.55; authorizing the Mayor to execute said Agreement on behalf of the City of Tampa; proving an effective date.
Memorandum from Brad L. Baird, P.E., Infrastructure and Mobility Administrator, transmitting additional information for said agenda item. (To be R/F)
agendaItems.background:
1. Contract Title: 24-C-09003-GMP01; FY 24 Citywide Distribution Watermain Improvements Design-Build a. Dollar amount: $19,890,062.55 b. Why the awardee was selected: Selected Pursuant to FS 287.055 CCNA.

2. Contractor/Firm: Westra Construction Corp.

3. Business Case: Project scope includes coordination and scheduling during the permitting and design phase, cost estimating, construction engineering and inspection (CEI), public relations, administering subcontracts and all related work required for a completed project.

Services will be provided under a task order contract for a negotiated guaranteed maximum price (GMP).

This Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP 1) provides for construction of approximately 34,000 lineal feet (LF) of 2-inch through 6-inch diameter water mains to replace aged, deteriorated, undersized, and substandard existing cast iron water mains that have surpassed their useful life. Proposed replacement mains are anticipated to consist of ductile iron pipe (DIP), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and/or high-density polyethylene (HDPE) in accordance with City of Tampa material specifications.

4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: The EBO subcontract contract goal for GMP-1 has been calculated and subsequently confirmed by the Goal Set Review Committee for an SLBE goal of 18%. The Design/Build contractor has acknowledged the narrowly tailored EBO participation goal.

5. Sustainability and Resiliency: Project provides for construction and public relations for various non-contiguous distribution water infrastructure improvements throughout the City’s water service area.

6. Community Engagement: The CAD Construction, Engineering and Inspection (CAD-CEI) team will assist the Contractor in the communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Build project. A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) • 608 consecutive calendar days.

• The Trimble project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

Resolution approving Contract Change Order 2 Renewal adding $3,349,124 to the Contract between the City of Tampa and Insituform Technologies, LLC for Contract 25-C-00012, construction of Wastewater Gravity Sewer Rehabilitation by Cured-in-Place Pipe (CIPP) – FY25; authorizing the Mayor of the City of Tampa to execute said Change Order on behalf of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
Memorandum from Brad L. Baird, P.E., Infrastructure and Mobility Administrator, transmitting additional information for said agenda item. (To be R/F)
agendaItems.background:
1. Contract Title: 25-C-00012 Wastewater Gravity Sewer Rehabilitation by Cured-In-Place Pipe (CIPP) – FY25 a. Address of Project: Various locations throughout the City.

b. Names of bidders/submitters: Insituform Technologies, LLC c. Dollar amount: • The Original Contract Amount was $3,349,124.00, • The Renewal Change Order 1 was an additional $3,349,124.00 for 1-year extension of the contract which brought the total Contract Amount to $6,698,248.00, • This Renewal Change Order 2 is an additional $3,349,124.00 which will bring the new total for the Contract to $10,047,372.00.

2. Contractor/Firm: Insituform Technologies, LLC

3.    Business Case: a. This project provided for the rehabilitation of gravity sewers from 8-inch diameter to 36-inch diameter at various locations throughout the City of Tampa Wastewater Department’s service area including cleaning, detuberculation and inspection, sewage bypass pumping, re-establishing service connections, lateral grouting post CIPP lining, maintenance of traffic, surface restoration, and all associated work required for a complete project in accordance with the contract.

b. The Renewal Change Order 1 provided for the first of two allowable one-year contract renewals. The work included cleaning, detuberculation and inspection, sewage bypass pumping, re-establishing service connections, lateral grouting post CIPP lining, maintenance of traffic, surface restoration, and all associated work required for a complete project. The time for completion was extended, the completion date was established as 03/24/2027.

c. This Renewal Change Order 2 provides for the second and final of two allowable one-year contract renewals. The work includes cleaning, detuberculation and inspection, sewage bypass pumping, re-establishing service connections, lateral grouting post CIPP lining, maintenance of traffic, surface restoration, and all associated work required for a complete project. The time for completion is extended, the completion date is established as 03/24/2028.

4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: To date, Insituform Technologies, LLC ., has utilized 1 city-certified firm for subcontracting participation.

5. Sustainability and Resiliency: The project serves to rehabilitate deteriorated and failing sewers in an expeditious manner.

6. Community Engagement: The Contract Administration Department’s Engineering and Inspection team will assist the Contractor in all communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a.    Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Bid-Build project.

b. Placemaking: N/A c.    Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget): • 365 consecutive calendar days with provisions for 2 (two) additional years at the same terms, prices and conditions.

• A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

• The Trimble Unity Construct project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. Trimble Unity Construct is a premier system for construction project management.
